name: Shelter Cove to Fort Bragg

map.locality_method: Outer-coast discovery extent from the Fort Bragg latitude band to the 40°10′ N Mendocino management line. Big Flat and Ten Mile protected-area rules need site review; this extent is not a fishing or navigation boundary.

harbor.name: Shelter Cove open-ocean boat launch
harbor.entrance_note: Shelter Cove is an exposed open-ocean launch, not an enclosed harbor. NOAA tide predictions do not clear the launch or approach; check the local operator, current conditions and chart before use.

source_names.H11971: NOAA H11971 / USGS dated Bear Landing camera research

bathymetry.reason: Original NOAA H11971 2 m MLLW BAG has qualified measured cells near 13 dated camera windows, but no full fishing polygon, current chart route or hazard clearance.

substrate.reason: One 2010 USGS camera archive documents five cobble and eight rock windows on two transects; it does not delimit a reef patch or current fish.

groundtruth.reason: Historical USGS camera windows include nine rockfish visual codes among 13 rock/cobble windows on two correlated transects; no catch-rate or current occupancy claim.

kelp.reason: Shelter Cove–Fort Bragg source coverage and local applicability have not yet passed the new-region review; a provider binding is a discovery lead only.

protected-areas.reason: The statewide CDFW geometry feed covers Big Flat and Ten Mile features, but exact area rules, nearby exceptions and launch-to-target access still need a local review.

regulations.reason: Mendocino species rules and five local protected-area source pages passed a new hash-bound review for this exact rectangle. A current date/position/method check remains required.

dynamic-closures.reason: Big Flat, Double Cone Rock, Ten Mile and MacKerricher MPAs plus the March–August Vizcaino no-entry closure are watched; live geometry and other exceptional notices still need each-trip checks.

wind-forecast.reason: NOAA GFS and ECMWF IFS responded for local forecast samples in the first regional rehearsal; exact issue times, matched hours and advisories still govern a trip.

wave-forecast.reason: NOAA GFS Wave and ECMWF WAM responded for local forecast samples; neither resolves the Shelter Cove launch or reef-scale seas.

wave-observations.reason: NDBC 46213 and 46014 returned observations in rehearsal, but are distant northern and southern references rather than Shelter Cove sensors.

weather-observations.reason: Buoys and NWS marine zones returned; KLLR is a distant land reference and no live Shelter Cove launch sensor was established.

tides.reason: NOAA 9418024 publishes Shelter Cove tide predictions; the observation station is historical and supplies no live launch condition or current.

surface-currents.reason: The NOAA/IOOS 6 km HFR request succeeded but returned no usable regional vectors. Do not infer calm or zero bottom drift.

subsurface-ocean.reason: Shelter Cove–Fort Bragg source coverage and local applicability have not yet passed the new-region review; a provider binding is a discovery lead only.

sea-temperature.reason: NOAA blended SST returned populated regional cells in the first daily rehearsal; this surface field is not a fish location.

chlorophyll.reason: NOAA VIIRS chlorophyll returned populated regional cells; cloudy or missing cells stay unavailable.

coverage_note: Limited Shelter Cove–Fort Bragg preview: seven official regional MPA/special-closure geometries, reviewed local rule sources, sampled GFS/IFS/WAM/GFS Wave forecasts, two distant buoys, Shelter Cove tide predictions and a dated H11971 seabed lead. No fishable targets, bottom images or exports; HFR vectors and live open-ocean launch clearance are unavailable.
landing_note: The 2010 H11971 camera rockfish sightings are research context, not present catch or a safe fishing route. Check Shelter Cove launch conditions and all local closures before travel.
